From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Patel <john.patel@atlasdata.com>, Priya Shah <priya@atlasdata.com>, Michael Lee <michael.lee@atlasdata.com>

Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Buying Committee Recap & Next Steps (AtlasData)

Thanks again for taking the time to join the demo today — appreciate the candid questions and the great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps to keep momentum:

Summary of attendees / roles (as we understood today):
- John Patel — VP Product (product/economic buyer contact)
- Priya Shah — Director, Data Platforms (technical lead)
- Michael Lee — CISO (security & compliance)
- Sara Collins — Procurement Lead (procurement/contract owner)

Top decision criteria called out:
- Performance: ability to support low-latency generation for interactive features (p95 < 350ms for typical 512-token queries)
- Cost: predictable unit economics for steady throughput (1M tokens/day baseline)
- Security & compliance: SOC 2 + evidence, VPC/private deployment options, data residency in US regions
- Integration: connectors to Snowflake and existing ETL pipelines; support for prefix caching and dedicated capacity

Agreed action items / owners / target dates:
1) Security artifacts: Marissa to share SOC2 checklist + demo recording (attached) — Marissa (today)
2) Procure & timing: Sara to confirm procurement window and PO requirements — Sara (by 2027-04-16)
3) Economic buyer intro: John to loop in CFO Lisa Morgan (requested) — John (by 2027-04-13)
4) Technical deep-dive / PoC sizing: Aditya to propose PoC topology and perf targets (dedicated pool or private) — Aditya (by 2027-04-14)
5) Mutual action plan: Marissa to create HubSpot MAP and include milestones/acceptance criteria — Marissa (by 2027-04-12)

Attachments & links: demo recording (Atlas_demo_recording.mp4), preliminary SOC2 checklist (SOX_Security_Checklist.pdf). HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ATL-2027-042

Next suggested touchpoints:
- Intro/approval with CFO Lisa Morgan once John confirms
- Security Q&A with Michael to review SOC2 artefacts and data residency
- Procurement sync with Sara to understand contract timeline and any redlines

If I missed anything, please flag. Otherwise I'll kick off the MAP today and schedule the technical follow-up with Aditya.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0172

Thanks Marissa — great session. A couple quick points from our side:

- Appreciate the recap. One clarification: the ultimate economic buyer will be our CFO, Lisa Morgan (I will intro her early next week).
- We need a ballpark on committed pricing for a 90-day PoC (expected ~1M tokens/day) — don't need a final contract number but a band for exec review.
- Security: SOC2 is required; we also need confirmation on data residency (we need US east). Michael, can you confirm any further items?
- Procurement: Sara will coordinate PO timelines but our internal target is to have procurement locked before month-end if possible.

Can you share the demo recording and the SOC2 checklist (saw the attachments) with Lisa when I loop her in?

Looping in a couple technical clarifications from our side to help with the PoC sizing and security conversation:

- PoC topology options: 1) Redwood Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) — best for predictable perf and isolation; 2) Redwood Private (VPC) if they require customer-managed network boundaries. Either works; we can size based on target qps and sequence lengths.
- Preliminary perf targets (based on 4xA100 equiv): ~ p95 280-320ms for 512-token gen, 1200 tokens/s throughput for batching workloads (numbers vary by model and quantization).
- Data residency: we can provision workloads in us-east-1 and provide audit logs + KMS integration for keys.
- Security artifacts: attaching a short performance matrix and a pointer to our SOC2 evidence bundle. Michael — happy to schedule a 30m security deep-dive to walk through actual artefacts.

Action: I'll draft a recommended PoC config (nodes, GPU type, expected token throughput) and share by 2027-04-14.
